codes.display: Screening for occult blood in feces (procedure)

remarks: FECAL IMMUNOCHEMICAL TEST
This test is used to detect trace amounts of blood in the stool that
is indicative of colorectal cancer. The estimated cutoff level for this
test is 100 ng/mL. Source: http://cebp.aacrjournals.org/content/20/2/272
Interestingly, if the patient previously had a positive test result (from
a malignant adenoma) the 'Malignant_Adenoma' PriorState will remain true.
If the patient is then later diagnosed with a benign adenoma the fecal test
will still return postive. This aligns with the likelihood of recurrent
adenomas being cancerous.

remarks: Following an initial prenatal visit there are 3 broad outcomes for a pregnancy:
1. Fetal Loss: 1.053M miscarriages --> 17.1% of all pregnancies
2. Induced Abortion: 1.103M induced abortions --> 17.9% of all pregnancies
3. Birth: 3.988M live births --> 65% of all pregnancies
Total pregnancies:  6.155M
Source: http://www.cdc.gov/nchs/data/hestat/pregnancy/2010_pregnancy_rates.htm
In terms of trends, the likelihood of abortion peaks age 20-30, then decreases with age.
Meanwhile, the likelihood of miscarriage significantly increases with age. 85% will
miscarriage in the first trimester, the remaining 15% in the second.
|     Age     |  Abortion %  | Miscarriage % |
Abortions source: https://www.cdc.gov/mmwr/volumes/65/ss/ss6512a1.htm

https://www.cancer.org/cancer/breast-cancer/treatment/surgery-for-breast-cancer.html
Surgery to remove breast cancer
There are two main types of surgery to remove breast cancer:

Breast-conserving surgery (also called a lumpectomy, quadrantectomy, partial mastectomy, or segmental mastectomy) – A surgery in which only the part of the breast containing the cancer is removed. The goal is to remove the cancer as well as some surrounding normal tissue. How much of the breast is removed depends on the size and location of the tumor and other factors.

Mastectomy – A surgery in which the entire breast is removed, including all of the breast tissue and sometimes other nearby tissues. There are several different types of mastectomies. Some women may also get a double mastectomy, in which both breasts are removed.
Choosing between breast-conserving surgery and mastectomy

Many women with early-stage cancers can choose between breast-conserving surgery (BCS) and mastectomy. The main advantage of BCS is that a woman keeps most of her breast. But in most cases she will also need radiation. Women who have mastectomy for early stage cancers are less likely to need radiation.
For some women, mastectomy may be a better option, because of the type of breast cancer, the large size of the tumor, previous treatment history, or certain other factors.

Some women might be worried that having a less extensive surgery might raise their risk of the cancer coming back. But the fact is, in most cases, mastectomy does not give you any better chance of long-term survival or a better outcome from treatment. Studies following thousands of women for more than 20 years show that when BCS can be done along with radiation, having a mastectomy instead does not provide any better chance of survival.

remarks: Immunohistochemistry (IHC), which detects the number of HER2 protein receptors in the cancer cells:
https://ww5.komen.org/BreastCancer/TumorCharacteristics.html

https://www.webmd.com/breast-cancer/breast-cancer-types-er-positive-her2-positive#1

All antibody-antigen interactions investigated in this study, both the primary antibody binding to its target and the secondary antibody binding to the primary, require several hours to reach equilibrium at the concentrations used:

remarks: A routine gynecological exam with a pap smear should be performed yearly for cervical cancer screening. Any abnormal vaginal spotting or bleeding should be reported to your primary care provider or gynecologist to evaluate for the possibility of uterine (endometrial) cancer, especially in women over the age of 50 and on tamoxifen. Although unusual vaginal bleeding can occur with menopause, any kind of vaginal bleeding after menopause should be checked out by your gynecologist or primary care provider.
https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/kimmel_cancer_center/centers/breast_cancer_program/treatment_and_services/survivorship/follow_up/pelvic_exams.html
If you take tamoxifen, tell your doctor about any unusual vaginal bleeding. If you take it and still have your uterus, you need an annual Pap smear, regardless of age.
https://www.webmd.com/breast-cancer/guide/breast-cancer-follow-up-care

guardDefinitions.education-topic-compatible: Preserve the actual counselling subject. Pregnancy counselling can concern a partner; it does not itself assert that this patient is pregnant.
guardDefinitions.time-window-compatible: Synthetic duration replaces the original procedure duration and is recorded separately. It must fit inside a known encounter and before death; an incompatible or unbounded encounter blocks duration enrichment.
guardDefinitions.deduplicate-session: One synthetic service per matching patient/encounter/topic/session; link all source events to that service.
guardDefinitions.candidate-method-compatible: Explicit source method has precedence. Choose a more specific or broader compatible method; any actual method replacement must be labeled as such.
guardDefinitions.context-selects-assessment: Geriatric requires age >=65; palliative requires palliative context; pulmonary/metabolic options require that clinical topic. A simple routine psychosocial interview can be synthesized for otherwise general consultations without asserting mental illness. A clearly organ-specific source excludes unrelated tests.
guardDefinitions.candidate-age-compatible: Apply the per-target age rules and keep source age; never create adult/geriatric services in children or neonatal services in adults.
guardDefinitions.developmental-method-age-compatible: School-age screening only; use the existing school/development context. Do not use neonatal metabolic screening as psychological testing.
guardDefinitions.cooperative-test-feasible: Require known age >=6 and no recognized coma, unconsciousness, acute respiratory failure or paralysis preventing the task. This is a synthetic dataset default, not a universal clinical cutoff.
guardDefinitions.neuromuscular-topic-compatible: A neurological or muscle-function question must fit the source event. EMG/neurography does not create epilepsy or a neuromuscular diagnosis.
guardDefinitions.anatomical-region-compatible: Use explicit body-site labels, then linked reasons, then active diagnostic context. Wound regions must be known and unambiguous. Organ/limb absence blocks these candidates. Source-specific restrictions fix explicitly encoded regions.
guardDefinitions.therapy-period-compatible: The proposed weekly treatment series must fit the existing episode. Assume professional setting and unrecorded units, but materialize their times and avoid overlap with death/discharge. Do not claim five units in a ten-minute event.
guardDefinitions.deduplicate-course: Merge source events belonging to the same therapy course; preserve all source IDs and count covered source events separately from emitted rows.
guardDefinitions.palliative-context: Existing hospice/palliative source event is sufficient. Other general examinations need palliative context; do not invent terminal illness.
guardDefinitions.monitoring-context-compatible: Source care/observation, perioperative, respiratory-support, ICU, specialty admission or vital-sign assessment can anchor a monitoring episode. A generic movement or administrative record alone cannot.
guardDefinitions.stress-test-compatible: Prefer resting TDI in acute illness. Stress echo requires a stable compatible cardiac evaluation; unknown technique can be assumed, explicit contraindicating context excludes stress.
guardDefinitions.contrast-compatible: Recognized contrast allergy or contraindication blocks enrichment.
guardDefinitions.pregnant-female-source: For this synthetic Synthea dataset require source Patient.gender=female, age 12..55 years at event and an existing pregnancy context, with no hysterectomy/absent uterus or conflicting anatomy. These are conservative project defaults, not universal rules about gender or fertility. Missing sex/age blocks maternal/fetal targets; do not infer them from a random draw.
guardDefinitions.gestational-stage-compatible: Recognized early-pregnancy or first-trimester context blocks replacing fetal viability assessment with anomaly work-up; no finding is generated.
guardDefinitions.anatomical-region-required: Resolve the clinical body region from the event, linked reason or same-encounter diagnostic question before selecting an organ-specific imaging target; otherwise keep source.
guardDefinitions.allergy-topic-required: An allergy-screening source is sufficient for assumed provocation; a tuberculosis test is handled by pathogen diagnostics instead.
guardDefinitions.pathogen-required: Source display/code or linked indication establishes organism/infection group. Preserve specimen/organ. Permit molecular replacement of culture/serology. Use resistance testing only for meaningful organism/clinical combinations; otherwise no-resistance candidate.
guardDefinitions.specimen-compatible: The assigned source group permits synthetic molecular replacement of the source assay. Source resources and specimen references remain unchanged; no specimen resource is generated.
guardDefinitions.hiv-context-required: Existing HIV follow-up/CD4 indication is required; source positivity/negativity and recorded viral-load results remain unchanged.
guardDefinitions.solid-tumour-context: HER2 testing in a solid-tumour work-up is required; never create a cancer diagnosis from a generic screening test.
guardDefinitions.deduplicate-stay: Emit one corresponding OPS per existing stay where applicable; retain repeated source services in provenance.
guardDefinitions.medication-route-compatible: Restricted source concepts permit an additional therapeutic injection service. Medication dose, route and intent resources remain unchanged.
guardDefinitions.renal-transplant-context: Kidney work-up/regime is sufficient. Generic transplant referral needs renal context; waiting-list admission is not assumed.
guardDefinitions.access-route-compatible: Explicit arterial access cannot become venous access. Known peripheral/central route wins. For unspecified access use peripheral by default; central candidate only in a compatible source surgical/ICU context.
guardDefinitions.deduplicate-access: Reuse a compatible existing catheter/access within the episode. A companion access proposal does not imply one new catheter per dose.
guardDefinitions.anaesthesia-compatible: Source-specific techniques fix candidates. Prior major operations in the episode exclude sedation-only replacement. Epidural candidates are restricted by the assigned source group.
guardDefinitions.airway-compatible: Actual source intubation is required. No emergency indication, tracheostomy or double-lumen tube is invented.
guardDefinitions.cast-region-compatible: Limb injury allows a synthetic elaborate cast. Jaw, rib and hip cases are excluded from this generic candidate; known side and region are retained.
guardDefinitions.knee-injury-context: Source knee operation/injury is required; preserve knee side and do not invent prosthesis or ligament replacement.
guardDefinitions.associated-operation-required: Link to the existing relevant operation; a supplementary reoperation code cannot be the only procedural content.
guardDefinitions.skin-incision-context: Incision must involve skin/subcutis and be a suitable standalone event. Do not use this code for cardiac, cranial or abdominal intracavitary work.
guardDefinitions.chest-access-compatible: Explicit median sternotomy selects 5-340.9; explicit thoracotomy selects 5-340.1. Other chest-wall surgery uses only a compatible access; do not substitute pleural drainage.
guardDefinitions.female-reproductive-context: Require source female sex, age 12..55 and no recorded prior hysterectomy/absent uterus. These are conservative synthetic dataset defaults.
guardDefinitions.contraception-context: Contraception source supplies intent; recognized active pregnancy and the shared reproductive anatomy/sex/age checks block candidates.
guardDefinitions.maternal-delivery-episode: Use the maternal record and an existing birth episode; no delivery on a newborn record, before pregnancy, or outside its birth episode. Caesarean context must not become normal vaginal delivery supervision.
guardDefinitions.deduplicate-birth: Aggregate induction/augmentation/birth events into a single compatible birth-supervision service; preserve operations separately.
guardDefinitions.ectopic-pregnancy-context: Require the existing ectopic-pregnancy/local methotrexate event; no normal pregnancy may be replaced by ectopic pregnancy.
guardDefinitions.dentition-compatible: Preserve tooth/jaw/appliance context and known dentition. No permanent-tooth appliance in a newborn or replacement of an explicit fixed appliance by removable equipment.
guardDefinitions.bowel-context-compatible: The assigned enema source concept supplies the bowel indication; source clinical resources remain unchanged.
guardDefinitions.metabolic-challenge-compatible: Glucose-screening context permits a synthetic challenge; no incompatible known acute metabolic state or explicit contraindication may be overridden.
guardDefinitions.wound-present: A real source wound or wound-care episode must exist. Minor devitalized tissue may be assumed; never invent a wound on intact skin.

order: validate source identity and global contradictions
apply explicit source facts and source-specific overrides
use deterministic choice only among remaining genuine alternatives
merge duplicate episode/stay services while preserving source provenance
selectionContract.serialization: Canonical UTF-8 JSON array with fixed field order, separators comma/colon, no whitespace; no display labels, input positions, report timestamps or global mapping hash.
selectionContract.selection: Sort candidates by stable ASCII IDs. Weights are positive integers. Let H be the unsigned big-endian 256-bit SHA-256 value and W total eligible weight. Bucket=floor(H*W/2^256); select the first cumulative weight strictly above bucket. This has at most 2^-256 discretization error; no floating-point calculation.
selectionContract.versioning: Record mapping file hash, rule revision and algorithm ID. Mapping hash and rule revision are audit metadata, not random seed components. Changes to candidates/conditions/weights can change that rule; unrelated rules do not perturb choices.
selectionContract.weights: Illustrative variety only; no epidemiological evidence claimed. Source-supported candidate overrides always beat weights.
selectionContract.identityFallback: A stable Procedure.id is required by the clinical importer. Missing identity produces a reported omission, never an order-based synthetic identity.
selectionContract.episodeConsistency: Resolve shared anatomy and patient facts from source references before event-level choices. Retain the source for ambiguous wound sites. Aggregate matching synthetic services by patient, encounter and target, using source IDs for stable ownership.
selectionContract.reuse: A companion service already present in the same episode is referenced/aggregated, not multiplied once per source event.

provenancePolicy.creationMethod: Human-readable clinical-topic grouping authored by an agent, then checked against the official OPS terminal catalogue. The choices are deliberate synthetic assumptions, not an automatic terminology crosswalk or a clinically validated equivalence map.
provenancePolicy.reconstructionLimit: Stored candidates, weights and selection contract reproduce event choices. Independent future reasoning is not guaranteed to recreate authored candidates or weights; preserve these decisions as versioned data.
endProductRequirements: Preserve per-concept provenance, assumptions, selection metadata and guards with the production mapping.

Use repository-relative paths and immutable upstream links.
Run scripts/audit_procedure_mapping.py against the pinned source checkout and official target catalogue.
Test missing provenance, invalid targets, unknown guards, changed fingerprints, event replay and contradictions.
Retain reasons for unmapped/excluded entries and honest review statuses.
